recommended_approach: Use a pre-fractured rigid-body workflow (Cell Fracture/Voronoi shards) and drive the shatter with rigid body collision from the brick. From the docs search results: use Triangle Mesh collision for detailed shard interactions (with the tradeoff that it is slower/less stable), set shard mesh margin to 0 when accuracy is needed, and bake the simulation before final render (Object Mode, cache/bake workflow) to avoid re-sim glitches.

key_parameters.collision_shape_shards: Mesh (triangle-only, supports concave geometry; more detailed interactions, but slower/less stable)
key_parameters.collision_shape_frame_wall: Passive collider (can use simpler/compound setup for stability)
key_parameters.collision_margin_triangle_mesh: 0 (docs indicate Active/Passive Triangle Mesh can typically use 0)
key_parameters.margin_guidance: Nonzero margin often improves stability/performance for many shapes; Triangle Mesh behaves differently
key_parameters.mesh_source_options: Base / Deform / Final (Final includes all deformations/modifiers)

surface_response.friction: Higher values increase resistance and reduce post-collision motion

key_parameters.bake_workflow: Use Bake / Bake All Dynamics and persistent cache before rendering

warnings: Triangle Mesh collision is more detailed but slower and generally less stable than primitive/convex approaches.
Increasing Cache Step reduces cache size but interpolates between stored frames and may deviate from original sim.
Baking can make Blender temporarily unresponsive; do sim baking before final renders.
Unnamed/ambiguous cache usage can cause conflicts across physics objects.
No API doc_refs found (expected bpy.types.* or bpy.ops.* references).
alternative_approaches: Use Convex Hull instead of Mesh when concavity is limited (faster/more stable).
Use Compound Parent built from primitive child colliders to approximate concave structures with better stability/performance.
